source_lines.98: 1.3 Fix a scale $r>0$, the rectangle $C=[-4r,4r]\times[0,4r]$, and the lower triangle with vertices $(-4r,0),(0,-4r),(4r,0)$. Their union is the fixed convex pentagon $D$. Keep its two lower triangles $K_\pm$ formed by the root $o=(0,0)$ unchanged. Inside $C$, choose a narrow positive-$x$ fan with consecutive outer vertices $v_j=R_j(\cos\theta_j,\sin\theta_j)$, $R_j\in\{r/2,r\}$ alternating, $\theta_j=\delta+j a/N$, and triangles $(o,v_j,v_{j+1})$, together with its reflection in the vertical axis. Use a fixed multiple of $N$ such sides and retain short end ramps in the same wedge. For $a\ll\delta\ll1$, their interiors are disjoint, their total area is comparable to $ar^2$, and the distance from $o$ to each long straight side is comparable to $ar/N$, by the exact determinant $R_jR_{j+1}\sin(a/N)$. On each side's middle third, its longitudinal coordinate from $o$ is comparable to $r$ and its clearance from nonincident fan edges is at least a fixed multiple of $ar/N$: scale a pair of neighboring alternating-radius triangles by that transverse distance; their fixed radial ratio and bounded middle-third parameter give this positive minimum directly. Place equally spaced attachment triples there at spacing $\ell\asymp b_0 ar/N$, each child radius $\rho r\asymp\sigma\ell$. Discard a fixed bounded number near ends and pair every choice by reflection. The total count is $B\asymp N^2/(b_0a)$; the boxes and their comparison windows are disjoint when $b_0,\sigma$ and the fixed window multiplier are sufficiently small. This explicit fan supplies the side/count hypotheses of part 2. All subsequent insertions are the finite conforming collar, guard and macrointerface constructions in that phase. [F1, F2, construct, algebra]
source_lines.112: 1.10 **6. Exact pressure lifts and no eighth boundary node**. Use the established logarithmic corner lifts inside the child. Refinement subdivides already assigned star regions and never increases their total area; it preserves all pressure-lift energies. No child boundary edge is subdivided, because these interfaces meet it only at the prescribed seven vertices. No projection on skinny cells is used. For a base pressure kink use the single lift selected by the preceding kernel argument, `F(t,n)=kappa |t-n|,` or its reflected partner kappa|t+n|. See the internal proof in part 17. The line t=n goes from root to the EXISTING top-right corner. Its traces are affine on EACH of the seven boundary edges: base kappa|t|, right side kappa(4r-n), left side kappa(4r+n), top kappa(4r-t). Thus no eighth top-edge node is needed. Its gradient cost is C|kappa|r. Protected near-base fans avoid the line and see exact affine pieces. Constrain the transition to this same macroline. On the SWNE uniform stencil the line is already a union of diagonal edges; its reflected lift uses NWSE. Cutoffs vary ONLY on the common uniform annulus. All coarse-zone values remain exact. Every parent pressure lift is affine throughout the complete selected child's ring neighborhood by the margin in Section 1. Thus neither uniform diagonals nor radial parent-guard refinements require a nonaffine pressure interface in the uniform ring. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]
source_lines.226: 1.67 **Part 13: Localized incoming cutoff and restored scattering.** **1. Precise geometric and boundary interface**. Assume the actual coarse transition/child lies inside a half-disc of radius r. Outside it there is a common uniform MINI mesh through radii 2r to 8r and on to the outer drivers. Let the geometric base be flat there. Prescribed pressure data on that base are treated as Dirichlet data; their pressure reactions are outputs. This is the local embedding problem, not a claim that the original global pressure has Dirichlet boundary conditions. Compare two incoming fields, one actual and one affine-background-plus-exact-short-layers, both satisfying the SAME uniform mixed equations away from their distant drivers. Their difference d=(v,p) is homogeneous on the common annulus. Its actual pressure and velocity traces on the base need not vanish. After subtracting an additive pressure gauge, assume that its reconstructed fields satisfy on the common annulus and a one-element enlargement `||v||_2+||grad p||_2+r^(-1)||p||_2 <= e r.            (1)` In addition, the actual boundary traces of d near the child must have actual MINI/pressure lifts of cost at most C e r. This last condition is automatic for zero residual base data, but is a separate interface obligation for an incoming kink or unequal base values. No trace hypothesis is inferred merely from an L² volume norm. The desired application of the independently derived incoming field estimate has e=O((r/R)A), where R is the distant-driver scale. The pressure potential error is O(r e), whereas velocity and pressure-gradient errors are O(e). This distinction avoids assigning a squared Taylor gain to velocity. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]
source_lines.262: 1.85 **2. A cheap kink lift preserving the seven-node boundary**. The literal function |x| would put a new node at the middle of the top boundary. Instead use the tilted crease `F(x,y)=|x-y|.                                         (2)` Its base trace is |x|. Its sole crease inside the box is the segment from the EXISTING root to the EXISTING top-right corner. On the other boundary edges it is affine: `left side: 4r+y, ; right side: 4r-y, ; top: 4r-x.` Thus (2) requires no eighth boundary node and no subdivision of an original seven-node boundary edge. Side-strip nodes simply carry the values of these affine traces. The other four pressure ports need not be zero: they are free interface variables in the glued comparison, and all induced internal loads are retained. Requiring them to be zero would be an unnecessary extra condition leading to the logarithmic corner-hat cost. The actual protected cones must lie on fixed sides of this crease. In the current convention, the right protected fan and its reserve holes lie in 0<y<x/3, while the mirrored left ones lie at x<0,y>0 with their corresponding near-horizontal aperture. Hence x-y is positive throughout the former and negative throughout the latter. The crease misses all protected fan interiors and all recursive holes. More invariantly, choose one of the existing top-corner rays from the root that avoids both protected cones; use the corresponding affine linear form that equals x on the base. This is the only macrozone condition used. Make that ray conforming by a finite intersection refinement outside the protected holes, if it is not already a macro edge. Intersections are interior to original boundary edges except at its two existing endpoints. Old P1 pressure lifts remain P1 under this refinement. The protected fans are untouched, so their actual sharp root-star lower bounds persist; refinement elsewhere cannot increase a vertex's original star area. Because F is affine on each whole recursive hole, every deeper copy is exact P1 there without further crease refinements. Once the template parameters are fixed there are finitely many new triangle shapes and the recursion-depth shape bound remains fixed. Extend kF through the child/coarse transition and turn it off only on the COMMON uniform annulus of radii comparable to r. Its crease is aligned with the southwest-to-northeast uniform diagonal in these local coordinates. Nodal interpolation of the cutoff product on that annulus has gradient bounded by C|k|: F=O(r), its gradient is bounded, and the cutoff derivative is O(1/r). Inside the child/transition no cutoff or interpolation is needed. Consequently the actual pressure lift Phi satisfies `Phi|base=k|x|, ; ||grad Phi||_2<=C r|k|, ; ||Phi||_2<=C r^2|k|.                                 (3)` The constants are independent of recursion depth, aperture, side-strip height, and coarse-element angles. The estimate is obtained from the explicit affine gradients, not an inverse inequality. A transition not yet conformed to the crease must be refined as above; that is an explicit geometric requirement, not an assumed estimate on its old mesh. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]
source_lines.282: 1.95 **2. A fixed macro correction around the seven-node child**. Construct a continuous piecewise-affine S, on a fixed child-scale macro subdivision, with `S=|x-y| throughout the child box, ; S=|x| outside S_(8r), ; S|base=|x|, ; |S|<=C r,  |grad S|<=C` on its correction support. Here the last size bound is only required where S differs from |x|. The construction is elementary: triangulate the fixed U-shaped polygon between the child rectangle and S_(8r), assign the inner trace |x-y| and outer trace |x|, and interpolate on a fixed nondegenerate macro triangulation. The top midpoint of S_(8r) is allowed as a uniform-grid node; no midpoint is inserted on the CHILD top edge. The child side-strip nodes lie on affine macro edges; inserting them does not change S on those macro triangles. Its gradients therefore remain bounded independently of the side-strip height. Inside the child use only the root-to-existing-top-right crease. This S is affine on each protected fan and whole reserve hole, as in the cheap kink-lift proof. Overlay its finite interfaces with the transition, never subdividing a child boundary edge. Refinement preserves old affine pressure lifts and does not enlarge any old vertex star. Outside S_(8r), the exact uniform grid is unchanged and S-|x| vanishes. Define before the distant cutoff `Psi(x,y)=g(x)+k[S(x,y)-|x|].                           (3)` Inside the child, (2) makes this exactly a x+k|x-y|. Thus the spurious vertical kink at x=0 cancels there, all seven boundary traces are affine, and no eighth node appears. Outside the child, the extra vertical g-breakpoint lines have |x|>=4r and never enter the child interior. On the uniform ring they are actual vertical lattice edges. The transition is conformed to those finitely many vertical interfaces and to the fixed S interfaces; it can be chosen before the pressure coefficients, since this is a finite linear trace space. No interpolation through a skinny triangle is invoked. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

source_lines.49: Assume Countable Choice for the H(curl), H(div), and real $L^2$ inner-product interfaces used here; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching tetrahedral mesh with realization $|\mathcal T|=\overline\Omega$. Define $C_k(\mathcal T;\mathbb R)$ by extending the oriented chain groups of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]] to real coefficients, and put $C^k=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(C_k,\mathbb R)$ with coboundary $\delta^k=\partial_{k+1}^*$. The degrees of freedom give a cochain isomorphism from
source_lines.51: to $C^0\xrightarrow{\delta^0}C^1\xrightarrow{\delta^1}C^2\xrightarrow{\delta^2}C^3$. Consequently the discrete cohomology in degree $k$ is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R),\mathbb R)$. If $\overline\Omega$ is nonempty, connected, and contractible, then the sequence is exact at every positive-degree space, $\ker\nabla$ consists of constants, and $\operatorname{div}:N_h^2\to N_h^3$ is onto. For general topology, define
source_lines.53: using the $L^2$ inner product. Then $\ker\operatorname{curl}=\nabla W_h^0\oplus\mathcal H_h^1$ and $\ker\operatorname{div}=\operatorname{curl}N_h^1\oplus\mathcal H_h^2$, with $\dim\mathcal H_h^k=\dim H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R)$ for $k=1,2$.
